Natalie — thanks, we can. I've attached a concise pricing matrix that lays out the three main axes: audit-log retention tiers (30/365/730d), key management (cloud KMS vs dedicated HSM seat), and residency (single-region vs multi-region). See attachment: redwood-compliance-pricing-matrix-v3.xlsx.

Quick notes:
- Audit logs: we price baseline retention (30d) as part of the platform; 365/730d are add-on line items priced as $X per GB/mo (see sheet "AuditLogTiers").
- KMS/HSM: KMS integrates with customer KMS (no recurring seat) and is billed per key ops; HSM is typically a monthly seat + per-request ops for attestation-heavy customers.
- Residency: single-region included; multi-region replication incurs a per-GB egress+replication fee and a small residency surcharge per region per month.

If you want, Ben from Sales Ops can put together the 3-year TCO scenarios you asked for — Ben, can you run 1: baseline incumbent parity (equal usage), 2: higher-usage delta (50% more tokens), 3: high-retention logs (730d) and return a one-pager?

Also copying Rishi for security/compliance economics — Rishi, if we make a concession path, what levers should we consider (credits amortized vs unit discount vs committed-seat credits)?

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Natalie — attached is a short 3-scenario TCO sheet (tabbed in the attached xlsx). High level observations:
- If ClearPath opts for 365d logs vs 30d, incremental annual cost ~ +24% on compliance line for our default usage profile.
- HSM seat economics become attractive once key ops exceed ~2M/mo; below that, a blended KMS + occasional HSM audit run is typically cheaper.
- For multi-region replication across two regions we model a ~+13% increase overall (egress + residency surcharge).

Laura (CS lead) — they asked about billing cadence. Would you accept amortized compliance credits over 12 months for a 24-month commit?

ben

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data protection package structure & economic benchmarking

Team — my recommended concession framework:
1) For enterprise deals we can offer a structured compliance credit instead of an upfront HSM discount. Example: $60k HSM credit over 24 months applied monthly as $2.5k/mo credit to the account, tied to a 24-month committed minimum spend. This preserves list pricing but reduces cash impact for the buyer.
2) Audit-log retention: offer a staged discount (Month 1–6: 0% additional discount, Month 7–24: 15% off audit-log line item) if they commit to a 24-month term.
3) Residency: waive first-region replication fee for the first 6 months of the pilot; multi-region surcharge thereafter.

Notes: HSM-seat vs per-op pricing comparison is included in hsm-seat-vs-usage-workback.pdf. If procurement pushes for a unit discount instead of credits, prefer credits — easier to reconcile with revenue and preserves negotiating room later.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Pricing & GTM Economics | Redwood Inference
